name: 24 GB consumer GPU (RTX 3090 / 4090 class)
arch: x86_64 host + discrete GPU, sm_86 / sm_89
notes: A class entry, not one SKU: 936 GB/s is the RTX 3090 floor, 1008 GB/s the RTX 4090. Setups listed against this class were reported by builders on either card.
Capacity is the binding constraint here, not bandwidth: 24 GB VRAM against 273 GB/s on DGX Spark means small models run much faster on this card and large models do not fit at all.
Nothing above ~24 GB resident fits without CPU offload. Qwen3.8-27B needs a 4-bit quant to stay on-card; BF16 does not fit.
No unified memory, so the disk-mapped embedding-table trick used for 100B+ MoE on Spark has no equivalent path here.

memory.note: dedicated VRAM on the card; host system RAM is separate and matters only for offload lanes. Class bandwidth spans 936-1008 GB/s; each variant carries its own.

compute.note: fp32_tflops at class level is the RTX 3090 floor; the RTX 4090 is 83 TFLOPS (see variants). Ampere (30-series) tensor cores have no native FP8 path — FP8 quantized kernels emulate through FP16 and pay for it; Ada (40-series) has native FP8.

thermal.note: 350 W is the RTX 3090 TGP; the RTX 4090 is 450 W (see variants)

variants.name: GeForce RTX 3090
variants.note: no native FP8/FP4 tensor path (Ampere 2nd-gen tensor cores)

variants.name: GeForce RTX 4090
variants.note: 1321 AI TOPS is NVIDIA's published tensor figure (FP8, with sparsity); dense FP8 TFLOPS not stated separately

sources.note: RTX 4090 official specs: 83 TFLOPS shader, 1321 AI TOPS tensor, 24 GB GDDR6X 384-bit, 450 W TGP
RTX 3090: 935.8 GB/s (marketing-rounded 936), 350 W, 35.6 TFLOPS FP32, 24 GB GDDR6X 384-bit
